colors.name: void
colors.role: ground — the dead screen before power; every signal exists against it

colors.name: glitch-white
colors.role: primary text, wordmark base, focus ring — the unsplit signal (17.9:1 on void, AAA)

colors.name: cyan
colors.role: accent + secondary text, links, ASCII bright band, focus halo (15.9:1 on void, AAA — carries text directly)

colors.name: red-shift
colors.role: the red channel of chromatic aberration; alert / error tag (5.17:1 on void, AA normal)

colors.name: blue-shift
colors.role: the blue channel of chromatic aberration; large/decorative ONLY (3.17:1 on void, AA large)

colors.name: cyan-dim
colors.role: cyan composited at 72% over void — secondary labels, the calm voice under the noise (6.51:1, AA+)

colors.name: mute
colors.role: tertiary text — timestamps, metadata, the operator muttering (7.37:1 on void, AAA normal)

colors.name: error-red
colors.role: decode-failed / corrupt block tags, slightly lifted from red-shift for legibility at small size (5.6:1)

colors.name: grid-line
colors.role: decorative only — hairline rules, clip-path tear edges, the faint scan grid (1.68:1, never functional text)

fonts.role: corrupted display — the RGB-split wordmark and section display; single-case geometric glyphs that read like a broken broadcast ident
the machine voice — body, track ledger, log lines, tabular timestamps; a grotesque monospace (not a CRT terminal face)
every Hangul glyph — a clean modern grotesque so Korean reads contemporary, deliberately distinct from PALE.SIGNAL's Nanum Gothic Coding

texture: Two fixed, pointer-transparent overlays sit above the content. (1) Scanlines: repeating-linear-gradient at 2px pitch — denser than PALE.SIGNAL's 3px CRT grille, the glitch aesthetic — 1px of rgba(240,240,245,0.05) ink every 2px, light enough that worst-case text contrast stays above AA. (2) Noise grain: a tiled data-uri SVG feTurbulence at 4% opacity over multiply, the datamosh shimmer. Beneath the overlays, the wordmark splits its red/blue channels every 4.2s for one frame (~16ms) and the whole content layer tears on a 7.7s cycle. All texture motion is removed under prefers-reduced-motion and the page becomes a still frame.

motion.name: ease-tear
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.85, 0, 0.15, 1) — clip-path reveals: violent in, settles hard

motion.name: ease-signal
motion.value: cubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) — fades and copy: fast, long tail

motion.name: clip-tear-in
motion.value: 520ms ease-tear, polygon(0 0,100% 0,100% 100%,0 100%) wipes with a 6px jagged step every 90ms so the edge reads as torn, not cut

motion.name: rgb-split-burst
motion.value: single-frame: text-shadow red -4px / blue +4px for ~16ms every 4.2s; resolves to a resting ±0.6px micro-shift

motion.name: ascii-scramble
motion.value: every 2.6s a 35% slice of glyphs re-randomize over 220ms (steps(4)) from a glitch glyph set; 65% of cells stay stable so the figure remains legible

motion.name: scan-drift
motion.value: scanline overlay translates 0 → -2px over 8.8s linear infinite (below 0.25Hz — photosafe)

motion.name: reveal-fade
motion.value: 480ms ease-signal, opacity 0→1 + translateY(10px)→0, 60ms stagger per observer batch

motion.name: cursor-blink
motion.value: 1.1s steps(2, jump-none) — the block cursor; below 1Hz, photosafe

motion.name: tear-jitter
motion.value: 7.7s cycle; one ~16ms segment of translateX(2px) skewX(-0.4deg) — content layer only, never the full-height scroll wrapper

motion.name: noise-shimmer
motion.value: 4% opacity SVG feTurbulence over multiply, static (no animation) — the datamosh grain
